data_output.description: data.encode(splits) remains unchanged and returns (encoded, dimension). encoded['train'] is (features, labels, users), encoded['valid'] is (features, labels, users), and encoded['test'] is (features, users). features is an int32 matrix in canonical source-row order; users contains the exact raw user_id values as strings. Trainer derives train_weights solely from encoded['train'][2]: for each row i, train_weights[i] = 1.0 / number of rows j for which str(train_users[j]) == str(train_users[i]). No validation or test rows participate in these counts.

model_input.description: Model.step(features, labels, sample_weights) requires aligned feature rows, float labels, and a one-dimensional finite strictly positive sample_weights array. It normalizes both weighted BCE and data gradient by sample_weights.sum() for the passed batch. Model.predict(features) remains logits in exactly input row order. The fixed training command must emit predictions_valid.npz and predictions_test.npz, each containing exactly row_ids and scores; row_ids are canonical sequential validation or test row indices and scores align identically.

model_designer.objective: Implement inverse-training-user-candidate-count weighted BCE in model.py while keeping the additive ID/context model and optimizer otherwise unchanged.
required_changes: Change Model.step in model.py to accept a third required argument named sample_weights aligned one-to-one with labels.
Validate that sample_weights is one-dimensional, has len(sample_weights) == len(labels), contains only finite strictly positive values, and has a finite positive sum; raise ValueError if not.

Compute normalized per-row gradient exactly as ((sigmoid(logits) - labels) * sample_weights / sample_weights.sum()).astype(np.float32). Use this gradient for np.add.at on feature weights and use gradient.sum() for the bias update.
Compute and return the weighted BCE exactly as -np.sum(sample_weights * (labels * np.log(probabilities + 1e-9) + (1 - labels) * np.log(1 - probabilities + 1e-9))) / sample_weights.sum().
Do not change Model.__init__, logits, predict, state, load_state, Adam constants, L2 treatment, feature handling, or model defaults.
preserve: Keep the existing additive sum of feature weights plus scalar bias architecture.
Keep L2 regularization applied to weight gradients only, exactly as in the parent.
Keep predict returning logits in input row order.
Do not add configuration-controlled loss behavior or alter any configured hyperparameter default in model.py.
coordination_notes: Trainer will call Model.step(features, labels, sample_weights) for every training batch, including the contract-check probe.
sample_weights are derived only from raw training user_id values supplied by data.encode as the third element of encoded['train']; model.py must not derive counts or inspect validation/test users.
The normalized batch-weight denominator is sample_weights.sum() for that actual batch, not batch length and not a full-training-set denominator.

trainer.objective: Update train.py to derive fixed training-user inverse-candidate-count weights from raw training user_id and pass them to the weighted Model.step API, without changing splits, features, optimizer settings, or validation-only checkpoint selection.
required_changes: Unpack encoded['train'] as train_features, train_labels, train_users instead of discarding the user array.

Before constructing or training batches, derive one weight per training row from train_users only: convert each user value with str(user), count its occurrences over the complete train_users array, and set train_weights[row_index] = 1.0 / count[str(train_users[row_index])]. Store train_weights as a finite positive np.float32 one-dimensional array aligned with train_features and train_labels.
In contract-check mode, call model.step(train_features[:probe_size], train_labels[:probe_size], train_weights[:probe_size]).
In the epoch batching loop, call model.step(train_features[batch], train_labels[batch], train_weights[batch]).

Retain the existing fixed output artifact names and write predictions_valid.npz and predictions_test.npz with exactly row_ids and scores. row_ids must remain np.arange(len(valid_features), dtype=np.int64) and np.arange(len(test_features), dtype=np.int64), respectively, so scores are in canonical encoded validation/test source row order.
Do not modify config.json; this ablation has no new configurable parameter.
preserve: Use only validation features, validation labels, and validation users for within_user_auc, checkpoint selection, and early stopping.
Never load, derive, inspect, or use test labels; test remains prediction-only.

Keep load(...), encode(...), all existing fields/features, training rows, date splits, RNG seed usage, batch size, optimizer hyperparameters, max epochs, patience, and valid_gauc_proxy improvement threshold unchanged.
Keep the command-line interface, including --contract-check behavior, unchanged.
coordination_notes: The sole raw identity used for weighting is exact raw field user_id already emitted by data.encode in encoded['train'][2]; no source-column alias or new data.py field is permitted.
Counts must be calculated once from the full training split before shuffling. A user's all training candidates therefore have total unnormalized weight 1 before per-batch normalization.
Coordinate with model_designer's required Model.step(features, labels, sample_weights) signature.

reasoning: This is a loss-only ablation. The training objective must balance each raw training user_id equally by assigning every one of that user's training candidates weight 1 divided by that user's complete training-row count, then normalizing the BCE and its gradient by total weight in each batch. data.py remains untouched because it already returns the exact raw user_id array for every encoded split. train.py must own weight derivation and API calls, while model.py must own the weighted loss and gradient implementation. Validation remains the exclusive early-stopping and checkpoint-selection split, and prediction artifacts retain canonical row order.
